pk/math.text: Explore and begin to make sense of their world through mathematical thinking and strategies.
Explore and begin to understand mathematical symbols and language in communicating their explorations and discoveries.
Develop an increasing ability to recognize mathematical problems in everyday situations at home and in the learning environment, and experiment to find possible solutions.
Counting: Explore numbers and number vocabulary with increasing understanding of their relationship to quantity.
Subitizing: Recognize and name the quantity of objects in a group without counting.
Comparing, Adding, and Subtracting Numbers: Begin to understand numbers as sets to be compared, put together, and taken apart.
Composing and Decomposing Numbers: Begin to understand that numbers are made up of smaller numbers.
Explore and begin to recognize the positional relationships between objects, their environment, and themselves.
Explore and begin to analyze two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes and shape attributes.
Investigate and begin to understand the concept of a whole and how it can be divided into two (or more) equal parts.
Recognizing and Building Patterns: Notice, recognize, copy, extend, and create repeating patterns.
Ordering and Seriation: Arrange objects in order according to changes in a specific attribute, such as size, length, number, color, etc.
Notice and recognize that things in their environment can be measured (length/height, weight, area, volume, temperature, time).
Compare things in their environment and use the language of measurement (lighter, darker, long, longer, big, bigger, etc.) to describe them.
Use non-standard and standard tools and units of measurement.
Recognize and classify things in their environment.
Sort things in their environment into groups based on attributes.

pk/language.text: Demonstrate understanding of increasingly complex language, including non-verbal cues.
Follow increasingly complex directions.
Communicate using increasingly understandable language, including sounds, gestures, signs, words, and language expressed using assistive devices.
Communicate using an expanding vocabulary.
Communicate using increasingly complex grammar and sentence structure.
Communicate with others for a variety of purposes.
Follow the social expectations of their personal cultural context when communicating with others.
Demonstrate interest in and care for books, including book handling concepts.
Demonstrate an understanding of print concepts.
Understand that print and pictures communicate ideas that can be read/viewed and understood by others.
Recognize letters, the names of letters, and how the letters are shaped, as well as some personally meaningful words.
Recognize the sounds associated with letters.
Notice, manipulate, and play with the sounds of language.
Recognize, manipulate, and play with sounds within words.
Demonstrate reading-like behaviors with familiar text or print materials.
Demonstrate an understanding of text.
Develop increasing control, strength, and coordination of small muscle groups.
With guidance and support, explore a variety of writing tools and materials.
Develop an understanding that writing is a way of communicating for a variety of purposes.
Show interest in using a variety of forms of early writing to convey meaning and represent sounds and words.

pk/science.text: Observe and investigate their environment using scientific thinking, scientific vocabulary, and the scientific method.
Observe, compare, and classify objects and information.
Communicate and/or record observations, questions, and predictions about their environment.
Explore and compare the ways objects move, including their speed, direction, and duration of movement.
Explore and observe the states of matter (liquids, solids, gasses) in their environment.
Observe and explore light and sound.
Explore and recognize a variety of earth materials in their community (soil, rocks, water, etc.) and their observable properties.
Recognize and identify different weather conditions and the ways weather can impact their lives.
Recognize and make connections between the seasons and their observable characteristics.
Explore, observe, notice, and describe a variety of plants and animals in their community, and their life cycles.
Observe and explore the habitats of a variety of plants and animals in their community (such as wooded areas, parks, lakes, and streams).
Observe, describe, and compare the differences between living and non-living things.

pk/social.text: Recognize themselves as unique individuals and become aware of the uniqueness of others.
Recognize themselves as members of a family and become aware of how families are alike and different.
Demonstrate a growing sense of belonging across their home, their learning environment, and their community.
Participate in the routines, customs, and traditions of their family and community, and develops an awareness of and respect for the ways these can differ across settings, families, and cultures.
Show a growing understanding of and participation with the expectations, boundaries, and responsibilities in their family, learning environment, and community.
Develop a growing understanding of what people need to thrive and the ways people fill those needs.
Develop a growing understanding of value, as well as supply and demand, as they relate to sharing and trading.
Explore and learn how to respectfully interact with nature.
Begin to identify, and use location vocabulary to describe, places and physical features in their environment.
Demonstrate a growing understanding of the passage of time as it impacts their lives.
Demonstrate awareness of and recognize the value of their personal traits, including their strengths and interests.
Demonstrate willingness to explore independently and try new things.
Express their emotions freely, and begin to identify and manage those emotions, with support from familiar adults.
Demonstrate flexibility and an increasing ability to adapt to changes and setbacks.
Recognize other people’s emotions and respond with care, sensitivity, and later empathy.
Recognize and respond to social cues.
Demonstrate an understanding that the diverse community of people around them have unique strengths and experiences to share and should be treated with respect.
Demonstrate healthy attachment to and trust in familiar adults in their lives.
Demonstrate an ability to initiate and sustain interactions and communication with others, primarily in their home language.

Develop and maintain deep, caring connections, friendships, and other relationships with people of various cultures, family structures, home languages, racial identities, genders and gender identities, abilities and disabilities, religious beliefs, and socio-economic classes.
Express disagreement and begin to manage conflict in safe, developmentally appropriate ways.
Begin to make choices that reflect their understanding of fairness and unfairness, as well as the boundaries and expectations of various situations.
Show a desire to positively participate in their community (family, learning environment, school, community) through showing care and consideration for others.
